title: Projectile Motion (flat ground, cliffs, inclined landing)
theory: Decompose: horizontal motion is uniform ($a_x=0$), vertical is uniform acceleration $-g$. The **time of flight comes from the vertical motion alone**; feed it into the horizontal. Impact angles come from velocity components, never from position. Three standard launches: angled from level ground, horizontal from a height, and off a cliff.

formulas.description: Level ground, speed — at angle $\theta$: flight time $t_f = \frac{2v\sin\theta}{g}$; range $L = \frac{2v^2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{g} = \frac{v^2\sin 2\theta}{g}$ (max at 45°); apex $H = \frac{v^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$.
Horizontal launch from height — $t = \sqrt{2h/g}$; $x = vt$; $v_y = gt = \sqrt{2gh}$; impact angle $\tan\theta = v_y/v_x$.

parts.parameters:
- Given: particle mass $m$ (irrelevant), launch speed $v$, angle $\theta$, gravity $g$.
- Find: horizontal distance $L$ to landing.
- Diagram: standard parabola from ground to ground.
parts.conclusion: Mass never enters projectile motion. Limit test: $\theta\to 0 \Rightarrow L\to 0$ — options (a)/(c)/(d)/(f) fail it or the $\theta\to90°$ twin. The identity $2\sin\theta\cos\theta=\sin2\theta$ is why 45° maximizes range.

problems.title: Impact angle of a horizontal launch

parts.parameters:
- Given: horizontal launch speed $v$ from height $h$; gravity $g$; $\theta$ = impact angle with ground.
- Find: $\tan\theta$.
- Diagram: half-parabola from a ledge of height $h$.
parts.conclusion: Dimension check: (m/s)/(m/s) — dimensionless ✓. Limits: $h\to0\Rightarrow\theta\to0$ ✓; $v\to0\Rightarrow\theta\to90°$ ✓. Pitfall: the impact angle uses *velocity* components, not the displacement ratio $h/x$.
